newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: FORECAST - Malaysia Nov trade balance seen in deficit.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Malaysia Nov trade balance seen in deficit.

text.p: Malaysia's trade balance for November 1996 is widely expected to show a deficit, economists said in a poll conducted by Reuters on Tuesday.

Economists from 10 research houses forecast on average a trade deficit of 148 million ringgit for November, although their estimates varied widely -- from a surplus of 700 million ringgit to a deficit of 700 million ringgit.
The government's Statistics Department is expected to announce the interim trade figures for November this week.
"Imports of some big-ticket items were deferred in the earlier months of the year. They are being cleared now," said Hwee San, economist with NatWest Markets in Singapore.
She said the imports would cause a deficit in November, but Malaysia would still end the year with a much lower than forecast trade gap.
Economist Song Seng Wun at HG Asia in Singapore said oil and gas machinery imports would be the major cause of a November deficit.
The poll forecast on average that Malaysia's trade deficit would be 1.28 billion ringgit in 1996 on the whole against the government's forecast of 5.2 billion.
The forecasts for the full year also varied sharply, from a deficit of 2.5 billion ringgit to a surplus of 500 million.
Malaysia has reported a trade deficit of 954.35 million ringgit for the 10 months to October 1996, against nearly 9.6 billion in the corresponding period in 1995.
Economists said several reasons were responsible for the improvement in the country's trade balance and, as a result, a narrowing of Malaysia's worrisome current account deficit.
"Malaysia has maintained firm interest rates and allowed the ringgit to appreciate, which has kept domestic demand in check," said Sim Moh Siong, economist with Citibank in Singapore.
"Export growth is starting to pick up, which should speed up the improvement in the trade balance, which has been benefitting from an even weaker import growth."
Most economists said if there was a change in the government's plans to import large items like aircraft, ships and machinery, the actual figure would be at wide variance with forecasts.
"Monthly volatility makes it difficult to predict trade numbers," said economist Vincent Low at JP Morgan in Singapore.
Last October, Malaysia reported a deficit of 773.4 million ringgit, against a surplus of 650.7 million in September.

According to Dilip Ratha, regional economist with W.I. Carr in Singapore, November would show a large surplus because the ringgit continued to appreciate against the yen, causing the import bill to shrink in ringgit terms.
"In November, Japan also showed a lower trade surplus against Malaysia in both ringgit and yen terms," he added.
"The only surprise factor will be if the government is making any adjustments for past trade deficits. Or if there is a lumpy import we don't know about."
-- Kuala Lumpur newsroom (603-230 8911)
